correctness.rationale: The explicit period-doubling recursion \(s_{2n}=1,\ s_{2n+1}=-s_n\) gives \(s_n=(-1)^{\nu_2(n+1)}\). Approximation by periodic residue-class observables, with error bounded by three classes of density \(2^{-K}\), makes the Haar expectation rigorous. For any three distinct sites, the \(2\)-adic distance valuations are exactly \((m,m,t)\) with \(t>m\). Splitting Haar measure by valuation <m and the two modulo-\(2^{m+1}\) residue branches yields \(\mathcal T=\frac13-\frac{4(-1)^m}{3\,2^t}\); the pair result follows by the corresponding two-case split. The Walsh expansion of the sign indicators yields all eight probabilities; elementary optimization over integer m,t proves exact zero/minimum/maximum cases. Actual package verifier on moduli \(2^9,2^{11},2^{13}\) performed 638 exact rational moment checks and 7,936 exact sign-probability checks, but the infinite conclusion rests on the measure argument, not finite enumeration. No unproved infinite enumeration or numerical inference is used.

value.rationale: Third-order correlations and sparse cylinder probabilities are natural invariants in symbolic dynamics and diffraction. The result collapses the infinite family of all triples of sampling times to just two \(2\)-adic valuation scales, providing exact joint probabilities, zeros, a negative extreme and a positive extreme with fully classified equality cases. This is a sharp global classification rather than a finite table, arbitrary slice, relabeling, or a routine numerical recomputation. It clarifies phase-sensitive third-order structure of a canonical pure-point subshift beyond its known pair autocorrelations. General exact-patch algorithms cover computability, but do not supply this globally uniform simplicity, which can guide three-site observation/design and comparisons of dynamical symbolic laws.
